newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy presses on with Albania force preparations.
newsitem.headline: Italy presses on with Albania force preparations.

text.p: Italy, vowing to investigate fully last week's sinking of an Albanian refugee boat, said the disaster would not affect its plans to lead a multinational force to the Balkan country.

"Although there are clearly those who cast doubt on our ability to organise such a complex mission, I believe the episode will not interfere with this problem," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters on Monday night.

"So many countries will participate in the operation directly. All have asked Italy to coordinate this action and Italy is ready for this responsibility and duty," said Prodi, who faces parliamentary questions on Wednesday.
The multinational security force is intended to protect humanitarian relief supplies to Albania.

Prodi said Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta would address a joint meeting of the defence and foreign affairs committees of the upper house of Parliament on Tuesday on the developments.
Andreatta will ask Tirana to name a panel of experts to assist in investigating Friday night's collision between an Albanian patrol boat and an Italian navy ship trying to persuade it to turn back.
Tirana says at least 83 people drowned in the disaster. Some survivors have suggested the Italian corvette bore down on them deliberately, charges Italy rejects.
There have also been questions about government orders to the navy to intercept Albanian refugee ships before they entered Italian waters to persuade them to turn back.
Italian centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi described the action as a blockade and called on Prodi's centre-left government to abandon it.

The boat that sank was crowded with families from the rebel-held southern Albanian port of Vlore, one that the multinational force is supposed to secure, and angry crowds there said they had added Italy to their list of enemies.
"We want no Italians in this town. We lost our families," said Gjergji Greni, 34, on Monday.
"If we see Italian soldiers in Vlore now, we'll all go crazy. We have a common blood here."
Italy has invited Albania to take part in a joint investigation into the tragedy and promised to make available documents to ensure the doubts are cleared up.

Admiral Guido Venturoni, the defence chief of staff, said Albanian Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj would arrive in Rome on Tuesday to discuss the sinking and the protection force. Other countries' representatives arrive on Wednesday.
Venturoni said the force should be of at least 5,000 men with Italy providing around 2,000.
He said France would send 900 to 1,000 men while Greece has said it would send around 700 and Spain 500. Portugal, Turkey, Romania and Hungary are also expected to contribute.
The force received United Nations approval on Friday and was approved by the Albanian parliament on Sunday.
